items.text: Most laws should be made by regions and local communities rather than at the national level.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Core subsidiarity claim about law-making; replaces fed-01's near-consensus roads/schools list. Mirrors fed-06.

items.text: Regional and national bodies should have only the powers that local communities agree to hand up to them.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Bottom-up confederal principle (anarchist, municipalist, confederalist); agentless. Rewritten from draft fed-04 per review; mirrors fed-07.

items.text: If a region's people think a national rule is wrong for their area, the region should be able to opt out of it.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Judgement moved into the condition (who decides fit) so it is not a ceiling item. Draft fed-06; pairs with fed-08.

items.text: If people in different regions deeply disagree about a moral question, each region should be able to set its own rule on it.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Moral-pluralism case for local rule, neutralised per review; watch item-total correlation for country-specific pro cross-loading. Pairs with fed-09.

items.text: If national authorities override decisions a region has made for itself, the region should be entitled to refuse to comply.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Strong nullification stance; 'elected' removed to avoid dem cross-loading. Mirrors fed-10.

items.text: Most laws should be made at the national level rather than region by region.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Replaces draft fed-08 (blind audit: uniformity alone was 'unclear'); now states where law-making authority sits. Mirrors fed-01.

items.text: Any powers held by regions should be on loan from the national level, which can take them back at any time.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Strong unitary-sovereignty view (Jacobin, unitary-monarchist, democratic-centralist); mirrors fed-02 in extremity.

items.text: If a crisis hits many regions at once, one central body should direct the response, even where some regions would choose otherwise.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Coordination argument; the 'even where' clause adds a real clash with regional choice so it is not consensus. Pairs with fed-03.

items.text: If national authorities judge that a region's law treats a minority unfairly, they should be able to overrule it.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Civil-rights case for central override; unfairness is now the centre's judgement, not a stated fact. Pairs with fed-04.

items.text: If a region refuses to follow national law, national authorities should be able to govern it directly until it complies.
items.note: A region is a state, province or similar part of a country.
items.rationale: Strong direct-rule stance, mirror of fed-05; some lib cross-loading accepted for the mirror. Bounded by 'until it complies'.
